pw_slow_hash.note: Uses Werkzeug's default method. Flask>=3.0 (requirements.txt:1) brings Werkzeug 3.x, where the default is salted scrypt.

token_csprng.note: Tokens come from the secrets module. Only a SHA-256 hash of each token is stored (app.py:233-234).

no_hardcoded_secret.note: No signing key or app secret appears anywhere. The only literal is a dummy password used to equalize login timing, not a secret.

token_expiry.evidence: app.py:114 "SELECT user_id FROM sessions WHERE token_hash=? AND expires_at>?"
token_expiry.note: expires_at is set to time.time() + TOKEN_LIFETIME, which is 30 days (app.py:14, app.py:234).

logout_revokes.evidence: app.py:244 db().execute("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE token_hash=?", (sha(token),))
logout_revokes.note: POST /api/logout deletes the session row on the server.

owner_checks.evidence: app.py:253 "SELECT * FROM notes WHERE id=? AND user_id=?"; app.py:301 "UPDATE notes SET ... WHERE id=? AND user_id=?"; app.py:313 "DELETE FROM notes WHERE id=? AND user_id=?"; app.py:321 r = own_note(uid, nid)
owner_checks.note: Read, update, delete, share and unshare are all limited by user_id.

share_token_strong.note: 24 random bytes is 192 bits, from a CSPRNG.

login_rate_limit.evidence: app.py:217 if count >= 10: return err("Too many failed attempts...", 429)
login_rate_limit.note: Allows 10 failures per (IP, email) in a 15-minute window. The counter is in memory and is wiped if it grows past 10,000 entries (app.py:224-225).

password_policy.evidence: app.py:188 if len(pw) < 8: return err("Password must be at least 8 characters", 400)

sql_parameterized.evidence: app.py:345 "SELECT title, body, updated_at FROM notes WHERE share_token=?", (token,)
sql_parameterized.note: Every query uses ? placeholders. None is built with string formatting.

xss_safe_render.evidence: static/app.js:11 for (const kid of kids) e.append(kid);
xss_safe_render.note: Titles and bodies are added with append(string), which creates text nodes (static/app.js:64, 66, 114). The code never uses innerHTML.

security_headers.note: An after_request hook sets these headers on every response.
